exposure: universal delayed umbilical cord clamping (DCC) protocol implementation
outcome: umbilical cord blood gas outcomes (ability to obtain paired arterial and venous samples, abnormal blood gases)
cohort: The study included 682 patients with singleton term gestations, with 341 delivered pre-protocol and 341 post-protocol implementation.
finding: The widespread use of delayed umbilical cord clamping was not associated with an increased risk of postpartum hemorrhage or other adverse maternal and neonatal outcomes, although it did decrease the ability to obtain paired arterial and venous umbilical cord blood gases.
